expected:
# A3 — neighbor's chassis_id changes after a manual topo.id / topo.link.manual was set on it
Expected (matches the use-case doc's predicted 🔴, and topology-t-model-prototype-spec.md's own
E-A3 experiment framing): the manual topo.id (on whatever host/placeholder it was set on) and
any topo.link.manual referencing the OLD c:<old-chassis> id become dangling — the assembler's
own diagnostics() should list them as "dangling references" (§5.6) once the old id no longer
appears in any live observation, because nothing re-keys a manual decision when its target's
identity changes. Test both variants: mgmt_ip present (still doesn't help, since mgmt_ip
clustering per §5.2 rule 2 only ever attaches a REPORTER's own chassis-less self-observation to
a cluster, never re-anchors an already-manually-tagged UNBOUND peer) and mgmt_ip absent.
actual: manual topo.id orphaned (placeholder host keeps its OLD identity, new chassis appears as a SEPARATE unbound node)=True; diagnostics.dangling flags it=False; mgmt_ip present=True
notes: Detachment confirmed, but diagnostics() does NOT surface it as 'dangling' -- the dangling check only looks at topo.id/topo.unbind values with NO current cluster at all; a topo.id that still resolves to SOME (now wrong) cluster isn't flagged. Gap in diagnostics, worth a follow-up BUG entry.
